explanation: One of Jacob's twelve sons and the main character in Genesis 44, who served as governor in Egypt.
A valuable drinking vessel that Joseph ordered to be placed in Benjamin's sack to test his brothers.
Joseph's eleven brothers, the sons of Jacob, who came to Egypt to buy grain during a famine.
Joseph's youngest brother, whom Joseph wanted to keep with him in Egypt.
The patriarch and father of Joseph and his brothers, also known as Israel.
The land where Joseph became governor after being sold into slavery by his brothers.
Food that the brothers came to Egypt to buy because of the famine in Canaan.
The container the brothers used to carry the grain they bought in Egypt, and where the silver cup was hidden.
A severe shortage of food that struck Canaan and forced Jacob's family to seek help in Egypt.
